wu: Food Charades: Teacher shows flashcards of food (dates, harira, msemen, orange juice), students mime and say 'I like/don't like' the food. Winner gets a sticker.
wuAlt: Food Bingo: Students mark 'like' or 'don't like' on a grid as teacher calls out foods.
Quick Quiz: Students stand if they like the food, sit if they don't (dates, milk, couscous).
pres: Teacher holds up suhoor/iftar flashcards, models 'I like dates for suhoor because they are sweet.' and 'I don't like milk for iftar because it is cold.' Students repeat in pairs. Teacher asks 'Do you like...?' to check understanding.
presAlt: Picture Story: Show a comic of a child eating suhoor/iftar, elicit 'I like/don't like' sentences.
Realia: Pass around a date, ask 'Do you like this?' and teach 'yum!/yuck!'
prac: Team Quiz Show: Teams take turns answering 'Do you like...?' for Ramadan foods. Correct answers get points. Teacher monitors for 'because' sentences.
pracAlt: Food Survey: Students walk around asking 'Do you like...?' and tally results on a worksheet.
Matching Game: Match food pictures to 'I like/don't like' cards.
ls: Listen and Draw: Teacher describes an iftar table ('I like msemen and tea. I don't like lentils.'), students draw and label 5 foods. Check drawings for accuracy.
re: Stand Up/Sit Down: Teacher says 'I like harira!', students stand. 'I don't like soup!', students sit. Fast-paced to re-energize.
prod: Iftar Table Craft: Students draw their ideal iftar table, label 5 foods, and write 'I like ___ because ___' for 2 foods. Present to group with 'This is my iftar. I like...'.
rw: Days-of-the-Week Fasting Chart: Students copy the days of the week, draw a sun for fasting days, and write 'I fast on Monday' for 2 days. Teacher checks spelling.
st: Goodbye Song: 'If You're Happy and You Know It' with verses 'If you like dates, clap your hands!' End with sticker chart and high-five line.
g: Students mime food and class guesses 'Do you like...?'
Teams answer 'Do you like...?' for Ramadan foods.
Students react to 'I like/don't like' statements.
Students ask 'Do you like...?' and tally results.
Draw and label foods, present to class.
diff: Fast finishers: Write 3 'I like/don't like' sentences about Ramadan.
Support learners: Trace food words and use sentence starters.
hw: Prepare 2 facts about food to tell the class (e.g., 'Dates are sweet.')
Draw your iftar table and label 5 foods in English.
Ask your family 'Do you like...?' for 3 foods and write the answers.
tip: Use local Ramadan foods (harira, msemen, dates) to build cultural connection and relevance for Moroccan learners.
